correctness.rationale: Complete proof with each quantified range: the quotient has q^(2d-1) vertices and d times as many edges; after square cells its fundamental group is the explicit period lattice. Nonzero periods in the axis lattice have length at least q^2; off-axis periods have length at least dq, and embedded coordinate/diagonal cycles attain these bounds. These are all simple cycles and generate the respective sublattices. The quotient lattice modulo coordinate periods has exact order q, while the ordinary graph stage is free of the Euler-rank. The standalone q=3,d=4 checker replay independently verified node count, degree, triangles, short lattice shell and embedded threshold cycles. Finite checks support, rather than prove, the general theorem.
